provenance.instrument: Wood Handbook: Wood as an Engineering Material, FPL-GTR-282 (2021)
provenance.scope: Tables 5-3b (woods grown in the United States), 5-4b (grown in Canada and imported) and 5-5b (imported other than from Canada), all inch-pound. Each row names its table in its "table" field.
provenance.columns: The three tables do not print the same columns. 5-4b prints no work to maximum load, impact bending, tension perpendicular or side hardness; 5-5b prints no impact bending or perpendicular values. Those cells are null.
provenance.scientific_names: Tables 5-3 and 5-4 print no binomials, so every scientific_name in a 5-3b or 5-4b row is null. Table 5-5 prints the botanical name beside the common name, and those rows carry it as printed; the four lauan-meranti sub-rows print none and are null.
provenance.groups: Table 5-4b splits its rows into Hardwoods and Softwoods; Tables 5-3b and 5-4b rows therefore carry a group. Table 5-5b prints no such split, so every 5-5b row has group null rather than a guess.

units.specific_gravity: ovendry weight, volume at the stated moisture content (Table 5-3b footnote b). Tables 5-4b and 5-5b print one specific gravity per species, so in those rows the value sits on the green state and the other state is null. 5-4b footnote a states the basis: ovendry weight, green volume. 5-5b states no basis.
units.moisture: green | 12 | 15 (percent moisture content, as the table prints it)
units.modulus_of_elasticity_basis: simply supported, center-loaded beam at a span-depth ratio of 14/1; increase by 10% to correct for shear deflection (footnote c)
units.sample_origin: AF is Africa; AM, America; AS, Asia (Table 5-5b footnote b)

douglas-fir-coast.note: Coast Douglas-fir grows in Oregon and Washington west of the Cascade summit; Interior West is California and the Oregon and Washington counties east of but adjacent to the summit; Interior North the rest of Oregon and Washington plus Idaho, Montana and Wyoming; Interior South is Utah, Colorado, Arizona and New Mexico (Table 5-3b footnote e).
